title: Red Light Therapy
summary: Should I buy a commercial red light therapy panel, get a budget knock-off, or build one myself? Investigating photobiomodulation for skin health, muscle recovery, and general wellness.

overview.what: Red light therapy (photobiomodulation) uses 660nm red and 850nm near-infrared light to stimulate mitochondrial ATP production via cytochrome c oxidase absorption. The result: enhanced cellular energy, reduced inflammation, and faster tissue repair.
overview.science_status: Biologically plausible with growing peer-reviewed support. Most studies are small but consistent. FDA cleared first PBM device for macular degeneration in Nov 2024. Still needs larger RCTs for many claims.
overview.key_metric: Aim for 20–60 J/cm² per session. At 50 mW/cm², a 10-min session delivers 30 J/cm².
overview.bottom_line: Start cheap to validate it works for your goals, then invest if warranted. Consistency matters more than device cost.

research.title: Controlled Trial: Red & NIR Light on Skin Collagen
research.finding: 136 volunteers showed significantly improved skin complexion, reduced roughness, and increased intradermal collagen density over 30 sessions vs controls.

research.title: Mechanisms of Photobiomodulation
research.journal: IEEE J. Selected Topics in Quantum Electronics
research.finding: Established cytochrome c oxidase as primary chromophore. Photon absorption dissociates inhibitory NO, increasing electron transport and ATP production.

research.title: Anti-Inflammatory Effects of Photobiomodulation
research.finding: PBM reduces pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6) and increases anti-inflammatory IL-10 via NF-κB pathway modulation.

research.title: LLLT on Muscle Tissue: Performance, Fatigue & Repair
research.authors: Ferraresi C, Huang YY, Hamblin MR
research.finding: LLLT before exercise increased VO2max, exercise time, and reduced creatine kinase (muscle damage marker) vs placebo.

research.title: Phototherapy Meta-Analysis: Exercise Recovery
research.finding: Meta-analysis of 16 RCTs confirmed phototherapy before exercise significantly increases reps, time to exhaustion, and reduces CK levels. PBM outperformed cryotherapy.

research.title: PBM Beyond Cytochrome c Oxidase
research.finding: Identifies additional chromophores including opsins and light-gated ion channels. Effects may involve microbiome and circadian biology.

research.title: Comprehensive Review: PBM on Skin (2024)
research.finding: Confirms PBM efficacy for skin rejuvenation, wound healing, and dermatological conditions. Field moving toward standardized dosimetry.

research.title: Stanford Medicine: What the Science Says
research.finding: Balanced institutional take: legitimate mechanisms and clinical evidence, but many consumer claims outpace the science. Promising but maturing.

research.title: DIY Your Own Red Light Therapy Gear
research.finding: Step-by-step DIY build using LED strips for ~$100. Simple approach but lower irradiance than commercial panels.

considerations.label: Irradiance
considerations.detail: Target 10–100+ mW/cm² at treatment distance. Claims >150 mW/cm² at 6"+ are likely inflated.

considerations.label: EMF
considerations.detail: Keep <0.5 μT at treatment distance. Premium panels shield; budget ones often don't. Test with a TriField meter ($150).

considerations.label: Flicker
considerations.detail: <1% excellent, <5% acceptable, >10% causes headaches. Test with phone slow-mo (240fps) — visible banding = bad.

considerations.label: FDA Status
considerations.detail: Class II CLEARED (not approved). Clearance ≠ efficacy validation, just 'substantially equivalent to existing device.'

considerations.label: Eye Safety
considerations.detail: 850nm NIR is invisible but hits retina. Always wear rated goggles, especially at close range.

considerations.label: Wavelength Accuracy
considerations.detail: ±10nm tolerance is normal. Binned LEDs are tighter (±5nm). Generic LEDs may be way off target.

notes:
Leaning toward starting with a Hooga HG300 ($159) to test if RLT actually helps before committing to a premium panel.

Key open questions:
- Am I primarily targeting skin or muscle recovery?
- Do I care enough about DIY to invest the time?
- Is EMF a real concern at these exposure levels or is it overblown?

General advice from research: consistency of use matters more than device cost. 10 min daily with a $150 panel beats owning a $1,500 panel you never use.
